roofing-calculator.name: Roofing Calculator
roofing-calculator.tagline: Estimate roof area, shingle squares, bundles, and underlayment rolls for any pitched roof.
roofing-calculator.metaTitle: Roofing Calculator – Shingle & Material Estimator | JaurTools
roofing-calculator.metaDescription: Free roofing calculator. Enter building size and roof pitch to estimate roof area, shingle squares, bundles and felt rolls — 100% in your browser.
roofing-calculator.keywords: roofing calculator, roof shingle calculator, roofing material estimator, roof area calculator, shingle bundle calculator
roofing-calculator.quickAnswer: Roof area equals the building footprint plus overhangs, multiplied by the slope factor for your roof pitch. Divide by 9.29 m² to get roofing squares (100 sq ft each), then multiply squares by 3 for shingle bundles. Add 10% waste for cutting and hips.
keyFacts: A roofing square is 100 square feet (9.29 m²) — the standard unit shingles are sold in.
Roof pitch is written as rise over a 12-unit run: 6/12 means the roof rises 6 units for every 12 units of horizontal run.
The slope factor converts flat footprint area into true sloped roof area: √(1 + (pitch/12)²).
One square of shingles usually needs 3 bundles of standard 3-tab shingles.
Underlayment (felt) rolls typically cover about 400 sq ft (37.16 m²) each.
Waste allowance of 10% is standard for simple gable roofs; complex roofs with hips and valleys need 15%.
howTo: Enter the building's length and width in meters (the wall footprint, not the roof).
Enter the roof pitch as rise per 12 (for example 6 for a 6/12 roof; 0 for a flat roof).
Enter the eave overhang — how far the roof extends past the walls, typically 0.3 to 0.6 m.
Set the waste percentage: 10% for simple roofs, more for cut-up roofs.
Read the roof area, squares to order, shingle bundles, and felt rolls — all rounded up.
roofing-calculator.formula:
Slope factor = √(1 + (pitch/12)²)
Roof area = (L + 2×overhang) × (W + 2×overhang) × slope factor
Squares = roof area ÷ 9.2903 m²
Bundles = squares × 3 (rounded up)
roofing-calculator.workedExample:
Building 10 m × 8 m, pitch 6/12, overhang 0.5 m, waste 10%.
Slope factor = √(1 + (6/12)²) = √1.25 = 1.118
Footprint with overhang = 11 × 9 = 99 m²
Roof area = 99 × 1.118 = 110.7 m²
Squares = 110.7 ÷ 9.2903 = 11.91 → with 10% waste = 13.11 → order 14 squares
Bundles = 14 × 3 = 42 bundles
Felt rolls = 110.7 ÷ 37.16 = 2.98 → 3 rolls
benefits: Prevents expensive under-ordering that stalls a roofing job mid-way.
Stops over-ordering: shingles are heavy, bulky, and often non-returnable.
Handles pitch math automatically — no manual trigonometry.
Works in metric with internationally standard square/bundle conversions.
limitations: Estimates a simple gable/hip footprint: dormers, skylights, and chimneys are not subtracted — measure and deduct large openings manually.
Bundle counts assume standard 3-tab shingles (3 bundles per square); architectural shingles often pack 4–5 bundles per square — check your product.
Does not include ridge caps, nails, flashing, or drip edge.
A planning estimate, not a contractor's quote: get a professional measurement before purchasing.

faqs.a: A square is 100 square feet (9.29 m²) of roof area. Shingles, underlayment, and roofing labor are commonly priced per square.
For every 12 units of horizontal distance, the roof rises 6 units. Higher pitch means a steeper roof and a larger slope factor, so more material.

faqs.q: How many bundles are in a square?
faqs.a: For standard 3-tab shingles, 3 bundles cover one square. Architectural (laminated) shingles vary — many need 4 bundles per square, so check the packaging.
Cutting shingles around edges, valleys, and hips creates offcuts. 10% covers simple roofs; complex roofs with many valleys need up to 15%.

faqs.q: Does this work for flat roofs?
faqs.a: Set pitch to 0 and the slope factor becomes 1, giving the flat area plus overhangs. Material types differ for flat roofs, but the area math is correct.
Small skylights can be ignored (the waste allowance covers them). For large dormers or chimneys, subtract their footprint area from the roof area manually.

labels.pitchHint: E.g. 6 for a 6/12 roof; 0 for flat.
labels.overhangHint: How far the roof extends past walls.
labels.roundNote: Order quantities are rounded up; waste is included in squares and bundles.
